notes: Modal is an active Python-first serverless cloud for production AI workloads. Its current platform covers inference endpoints, model serving, training and fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, parallel batch processing, data pipelines, and isolated Sandboxes for coding agents and untrusted code.

The official documentation says Modal can deploy Python applications that can be containerized, and highlights compute-intensive workloads that benefit from horizontal scaling. It provides GPU/CPU containers, volumes, web functions, servers, queues, autoscaling, logs and metrics.
The Python SDK release notes show version 1.6.3 dated 2026-10-27, with new Image Builder and CLI/endpoint capabilities, confirming active development.

The Starter plan is $0 plus compute usage per month and includes $30/month of compute credits, up to three workspace seats, 100 containers and 10 GPU concurrency. Team is $250/month plus compute, includes $100/month compute credits, unlimited seats, 5,000 containers and 50 GPU concurrency. Enterprise pricing is custom.

Compute for Functions and Sandboxes is metered by the second for CPU, memory and GPU. The $30 Starter and $100 Team included compute credits do not cover Shared Endpoints, which are token-billed from the first request. Region selection can cost 1.15–1.75x base rates and non-preemptible execution costs 3x base rates.

Modal is developer infrastructure, not a no-code app builder. Python and cloud/ML engineering skills are expected; users should configure workspace budgets and estimate GPU, memory, region and token costs before production use.
